zh.CATEGORY: AI 语音生成 / 语音智能体（ai-voice-agents · text-to-speech）
zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它卖的不是「配音」，是「一段声音可以被复制、编辑、搬进任何场景」；音质是它的城墙，积分制是最常被骂的那道门槛。
zh.USER_SCALE: 可核实：官网自述 90+ 语言、17,500+ 声音；Product Hunt 4.9 分 / 236 条评论 / 44K 关注 / 29 次发布（2023 年上线）；官网 Enterprise 区列出的客户可核实到 Twilio、Disney、Stripe、Cisco、NVIDIA、Meta、Zoom、Klarna、Salesforce、Adobe、IBM、Deutsche Telekom 等。口径提醒：PH 描述写 70+ 语言、官网写 90+，两者不一致，本卡各自按原文引用。G2 本次抓取失败，不引用其分数；官方未披露 ARR、用户数与付费数，本卡不编。
zh.STAGE_MATURITY: 成熟期。产品已切成三块：ElevenCreative（TTS、声音克隆、配音、音乐、音效，另有图片与视频工具）、ElevenAgents（电话 / 网页 / WhatsApp 的语音智能体，带测试、护栏、工作流、分析）、ElevenAPI（语音、音乐、音效、配音、转写接口，含 MCP 服务）。模型线从 2023-08 的 Multilingual v2 走到 2026-09 的 Eleven v4，中间有 Turbo v2、Flash v2.5、Scribe 转写系列、Music v2 与 Dubbing v2（2026-05）。
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: 积分制订阅 + 企业年框 + 创业扶持。六档：Free $0（10k 积分/月）、Starter 首月 $1 后 $6（30k）、Creator 首月 $11 后 $22（121k，推荐位）、Pro $99（600k）、Scale $299（1.8M，3 席位）、Business $990（6M，10 席位），Enterprise 另议；年付黑五最高省 55%；创业项目 12 个月免费、33M 字符。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: 它是语音这一层的「模型 + 组件库 + 插座」：声音可克隆、可复用、按字符计费。墙不在功能表，在音质最后那点「像人」，以及中文场景里别人更便宜。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 按拔电测试判为原生型：拿走语音模型，只剩编辑器、声音库、接口与计费——产品立刻空壳化。所以门槛同时写在两侧：模型侧是音色、情绪、韵律的保真度；价格侧是积分换算成分钟、越用越便宜但要先预付。实测（燃冰）一句话最准：它像声音组件库——组件越全，越说明它卖的是零件而不是成品。
zh.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: 音质是它唯一不可替代的东西
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: 评论里夸得最多的三件事指向同一个点：自然（60 次计数）、克隆真实（22）、多语种（15）。而抱怨最具体的一条也指向它：长文本、跨会话的同一把声音会漂，数字与缩写要手动拼成字母才读对。用户愿意为「像」付钱，也会因为「不像同一个」立刻走人。
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 实测三问的结论：值这个价，因为声音可复制、还能在声音市场里交易；门槛在模型与声音数据的积累，不在交互设计。界面只负责让你把稿子贴进去，决定成败的是模型对情感、口音、长句的处理。这和 010 Fathom（门槛在识别）是同一类结论：AI 产品的墙都在模型那一侧。
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 最脆的梁有三根：积分计费、中文本地化、开源与大厂追平
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: 第一根：1 星差评集中在积分——页面写按月，实际按积分扣，两条 2 分钟语音扣 50,000 积分，客服 48 小时未回。第二根：中文要外挂（实测原话：中文配音 MiniMax 更便宜、更符合中文习惯）。第三根：Deepgram、Cartesia Sonic、Fish Audio 都在同一栏，差距在缩小，价格在往下走。
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: ElevenLabs 是一个 AI 语音公司：用文本转语音、声音克隆、配音、音乐与转写模型，把文字变成可复用的人声，再把能力拆成三种交付——创作者用的网页工作台（ElevenCreative）、企业用的语音智能体（ElevenAgents）、开发者用的接口（ElevenAPI，含 MCP 服务）。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官方一句（PH 描述原文）：Create natural AI voices instantly in any language。翻成用户语言：一段稿子贴进去，几秒出来一段能直接播的人声，还能换成经授权的任何音色、任何语言。
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 个人创作者（播客、有声书、短视频、解说）
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: 原来要自己录或花钱请配音，改稿就要重录。实测（燃冰）就落在这一层，判断是「定位更多地面向创作者」：免费 1 万积分够试，主推档 $22。评论也在这层最密：把 plan → script → recording → post 压成一步，两天的活变半天。
zh.SEGMENT_2_NAME: 开发者与产品团队（API 优先）
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: 不买界面，买接口：语音、转写、配音、音乐与智能体的 API，加 MCP 服务（api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp）。评论里 API 集成被提及 14 次，是他们选它的主因之一；这一层买的是延迟（Flash 75ms）与并发（档位 10 → 6000）。
zh.SEGMENT_3_NAME: 企业（客服、游戏、媒体、无障碍）
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: 看三样：合规（内容审核、责任归属、出处标识 Provenance，能判断一段音频是否 AI 生成）、语音智能体能不能接电话与 WhatsApp、大客户名单带来的采购安全感（官网列 Twilio、Disney、Stripe、Cisco、NVIDIA、Meta、Zoom、Salesforce、Adobe 等）。
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 把一段文字变成能播的人声，并且能换人、换语言、换情绪，不用重录。
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 改稿不用重录——不用再对着麦克风把同一句念第五遍。
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 作品听起来像有预算的团队做的；一个人也能给出「有配音」的成品。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 稿子改了一个字却要重录整段；或者要做多语言版本，而自己只会中文。
zh.FREQUENCY: 按内容生产节奏走：创作者一周几次到每天；智能体场景是 7×24 常驻（[推断] 依据是 Agents 按并发与分钟计费，官方未披露调用频次）。
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 网页工作台里贴稿、选声音、调参数、导出；开发者在自己的产品里调 API；企业把声音接进电话客服、游戏对白、视频本地化与有声书流水线。
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 触发点不是「我要用 AI」，而是「这段词要变成声音，但我不想录」——录制这件事的边际成本是嗓子。
zh.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: 贴稿 → 选声音 → 调 → 生成
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 实测路径：先在 landing page 看懂它卖什么，再进工作台；选库里的声音或克隆自己的，贴稿生成。摩擦很具体：流程里老报错，而且常在关键动作前撞到收费提示（原话：老是触发收费）。
zh.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: 几秒后拿到一段能直接播的音频
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: 实测结论：可以直接用；要改也能改，但要收费。要改的往往是「性格」这一块——录了自己的声音，生成出来却不像自己。
zh.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: 声音存下来了，下次不用重配
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 回来不是「再生成一次」，而是「我的声音、我的项目、我的历史稿子都在这儿」。克隆一次可长期复用，这是它留人的真实机制，也是它与「一次性配音外包」的分界。
zh.LOOP_FREQ: 按内容生产节奏：一周 3–10 次（[推断] 依据是创作者更新频率与 10k/月的免费额度，官方未披露）。
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 同一个动作反复出现：稿子定了就要出声音。它把这件事从「约棚、录、剪」压成「贴、选、导」。
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 它真正教用户的是「声音可以存成资产」——用过一次之后，人会开始为不同栏目养不同的嗓子，而不是每次去找配音。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 三条同时跑：口碑与作品外溢（用它的声音做出来的内容自带「这声音哪来的」）；模型发布节奏（29 次发布、44K 关注，每次新模型都是一次事件）；开发者生态与集成目录（API、MCP、以及用户讨论替代方案时它总被提名）。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 第一次听到自己的声音说另一种语言——克隆与多语种叠加的那一下。实测没计时，但记录的第一反应是「可以提取我的声音覆盖到不同场景」。
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 有，但属于作品型传播：做出来的音频在播客、短视频、游戏里被听到，听的人问「这是谁配的」。它不是靠分享链接拉新（生成结果不天然带入水印式入口），[推断] 官网未披露分享带来的转化。
zh.RETENTION_1: 克隆的声音与历史项目沉在账号里，迁走等于把声音资产重做一遍。
zh.RETENTION_2: 团队工作区与 API key 一旦接进产品，替换成本是改代码与重新调参，不是点几下。
zh.RETENTION_3: 模型迭代带来「越用越好听」——同一把声音在 v3、v4 上重生成会更自然，老用户有理由回来重做旧内容（[推断] 依据：官网模型时间线与版本升级公告）。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: 新模型（v3 → v4、Music v2、Dubbing v2）→ 老用户回来重做 → 作品外溢 → 新用户试用 → 免费 10k 积分撞墙 → 转付费。这条环的强度押在「每次升级都听得出来」上。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: 开发者先用 API 做一个小功能（一条 TTS）→ 上线后用量涨 → 并发与字符额度不够 → 升档或谈企业价。一旦接进产品，它就是基础设施，替换成本从「不喜欢」变成「要排期」。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 主入口。贴稿、选声音、调稳定性与相似度、生成、导出；模型档位（v3 / v4 / Flash / Turbo）决定延迟与自然度，实测里最常撞到收费提示的也是这一层。
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 护城河所在。17,500+ 声音可直接用，克隆把自己的声音变成可复用资产；实测说它像声音组件库，指的就是这一层。
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: 把音视频整段换语言并保留原说话人的音色与节奏，Dubbing v2 是 2026-05 的更新。这一层卖的是「不用重录就能出海」。
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: 从人声扩到「声音的一切」：配乐与音效，2025-08 上线 Music、2026-05 出 Music v2。对创作者是省一笔版权费，对它是抬 ARPU。
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 从生成内容转向实时对话：电话、网页、WhatsApp，带测试、护栏、工作流与分析。这一层收分钟与并发，是它把 To C 工具变成 To B 基础设施的那一步。
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 钱与锁都在这层：按字符与分钟计费、并发与席位分档、MCP 让 Claude 与 ChatGPT 直接调。定价页的槽位切分（3 / 10 / 30 / 160 / 660 / 2200 个音色位）比功能表更能说明商业意图。
zh.ENTITY_1: Voice（一把可复用的声音，克隆或库选）
zh.ENTITY_2: Project / Generation（一次生成，可回听、可导出）
zh.ENTITY_3: Credit（积分，钱的最小单位，由字符与分钟折算）
zh.ENTITY_4: Agent（一个能接电话的语音智能体）
zh.ENTITY_5: Workspace / Seat（团队、并发与权限的边界）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 主轴是「声音」：库里的声音或自己的克隆进项目，项目里出生成结果，结果按用途（视频、有声书、游戏、电话）分流。好处是复利——声音越攒越值钱；代价是产品没有天然终点，用户永远停在生成，要自己去外面拼成成品。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 实测（燃冰）路径：landing page 先看懂场景（官网按游戏、对话、旁白、角色、教育等切）→ 进工作台 → 选声音或克隆 → 贴稿生成。界面学习成本低，卡点在两处：流程里偶发报错，以及频繁撞到付费墙（原话：老是触发收费）。
zh.CRAFT_1_NAME: 按用途定价的问卷式入口
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: 定价页先问「你想用它做什么」（创作者、播客有声书、营销广告、影视、音乐音效、游戏、教育可及性、配音、个人），再给档位。实测注意到了这一点：它不让你比价格，而是先让你认领场景——把「贵不贵」换成「够不够用」。
zh.CRAFT_2_NAME: 把「像不像本人」做成两个旋钮
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: 稳定性与相似度分开给，是这类产品最实用的设计：要稳（长文本不变调）就牺牲一点相似，要像就接受偶尔漂移。实测的抱怨（听起来不像自己）本质上就是这两个旋钮没调对，而产品把它交给用户自己解。
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: 能判断一段音频是否 AI 生成。实测的评价是「这点挺好」——在一个会被滥用的品类里主动给输出打标记，是对长期信任的投资，也是企业采购的入场券。
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 先给够用的免费，再按用量收紧
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: 免费 10k 积分/月，刚好够验证几条；一旦日更就必然撞墙。它不是按功能设墙（功能基本全开），而是按用量设墙——试用体验完整，但「什么时候该付钱」变模糊，1 星的积分困惑就长在这儿。
zh.CRAFT_5_NAME: 声音市场把用户变成供给方
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: 实测记下一个细节：它建了可交易的声音市场，创作者的作品能在那里获得收入。意义不在抽成，在把「声音供给」外包给用户，让自己从工具变成交易所（[推断] 网络效应强弱取决于分成与授权规则，官网未披露条款）。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 先把「像人」做到没人怀疑，再谈工作流。所有工艺选择都在减少「一听就知道是 AI」的那一下，而不是增加功能按钮。
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：本次未测（实测只记流程顺序：看懂场景 → 进工作台 → 选声音 → 贴稿 → 出音频，未计时）
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 实测记的是结果不是秒表。本报告不把它换算成分钟，也不编评分。
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：低（工作台直观，贴稿即出；难点在「调哪个旋钮」而不是「在哪」）
zh.DELIGHT_1: 克隆一次，长期复用：录一段自己的声音，之后所有稿子都能用这把嗓子。
zh.DELIGHT_2: 一个人干出一支配音团队的活：多语种、多角色、多情绪，不用约棚。
zh.DELIGHT_3: 出处标识与内容审核都在，不做「假装看不见」的生意（实测评价：这点挺好）。
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜点：声音资产化 + 多语种即取即用 + 主动标识 AI 生成
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任：产品层有 4.9 分 / 236 条评论撑着，合规侧有内容审核、责任归属与出处标识；短板是计费透明度——1 星差评说页面写按月、实际按积分扣，客服 48 小时未回。
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 计费困惑：写按月、按积分扣；两条 2 分钟语音扣 50,000 积分（1 星差评原话方向）。
zh.STRUGGLE_2: 长文本与跨会话一致性：同一把声音在不同段落、不同会话里会漂；数字与缩写要手动拼写才读对（评论 Cons）。
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 中文与口音：中文支持弱被点名 2 次；实测的替代方案是 MiniMax（更便宜、更符合中文习惯）。
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 摩擦：积分计费、长文本一致性、中文与口音
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: 积分订阅 + 企业年框 + 生态
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: 六档订阅（$0 / 6 / 22 / 99 / 299 / 990，Starter 首月 $1、Creator 首月 $11）+ 企业年框；单位价格随档位下降（额外一分钟约 $0.36 → $0.17），音色槽位 3 → 2200，并发 10 → 6000。
zh.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: 入口便宜到 1 美元，钱收在用量与企业上
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: 首月 $1 的 Starter 与 $11 的 Creator，本质是把「试」变成「订」；真正的钱在 Pro 以上的用量档、Scale 与 Business 的席位与并发、以及企业年框。积分制让收入随用量自然增长，也让「用超了」成为常态投诉点。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: 免费：10k 积分/月、声音库可用、克隆有额度限制、商用需按档位授权；付费：更高积分、更多音色槽位、更高并发、192kbps 高保真、商用授权、团队与优先支持。墙不在功能，在「量」与「授权」。
zh.UX_MON_HEADLINE: 体验与变现是对齐的，还是打架的？
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 半对齐。对齐的一面：生成动作零学习成本，免费额度刚好让人尝到「像人」的甜头，付费点落在量、并发、授权这些「用起来才会缺」的东西上。打架的一面：所有高级动作（改性格、重生成、导出高品质）都在付费墙后，实测的感受是「老是触发收费」——顺滑与克制在这里是反向的。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 开发者与企业，要 ASR / 语音接口的那批人
zh.COMP_1_D2: ASR 起家（转写为主），TTS 是补位；PH 产品页一句 Voice AI platform for developers
zh.COMP_1_D3: 开发者文档与云市场，接口侧口碑
zh.COMP_1_D4: 按用量计价为主；本次未读取其定价页原文，不编价格
zh.COMP_2_D1: 要低延迟实时语音的开发者
zh.COMP_2_D2: 自研实时语音模型，卖点是快（PH 一句 Sonic is the fastest human-like voice API；具体毫秒数未在官网核实）
zh.COMP_2_D3: 开发者社区与实时对话场景
zh.COMP_2_D4: 本次未读取定价页，不编价格
zh.COMP_3_D1: 想便宜、想自己部署的声音克隆用户
zh.COMP_3_D2: 开源 TTS 路线（PH 一句 Expressive Text-to-Speech and Voice Cloning），可自托管
zh.COMP_3_D4: 开源免费 + 托管付费；本次未读原文，不编价格
zh.COMP_4_NAME: 云厂 TTS（Amazon Polly / Google Cloud TTS / PlayHT）
zh.COMP_4_D1: 已经在云上的企业与开发者
zh.COMP_4_D2: 通用 TTS，稳但不追求「像人」；评论里被点名为它的替代
zh.COMP_4_D3: 云平台的既有账单与目录，零获客成本
zh.COMP_4_D4: 按字符计价、随云账单出，用户感知为「本来就有」
zh.COMP_OWN_D1: AI 语音生成与语音智能体
zh.COMP_OWN_D2: 自研 TTS / STT / 音乐 / 配音模型 + 声音克隆 + 17,500 声音库 + 智能体编排 + API / MCP
zh.COMP_OWN_D3: 作品外溢、PH 29 次发布、开发者接口、企业客户名单
zh.COMP_INTRO: 名单取自三处：PH 的 Similar Products（Deepgram、Cartesia Sonic、Fish Audio、Vapi、Rask AI）、评论里用户自己说的替代（Amazon Polly、Google Cloud TTS、PlayHT、Cartesia Sonic）、实测（燃冰）点的中文替代（MiniMax、HeyGen）。竞品定价页本次未逐一读取，没读到的价格一律不写。
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 两处短期难补：一是音质与情感表现（好评集中在自然与克隆真实，这是模型与数据积累的差）；二是三种交付形态同时存在——创作者买界面、开发者买接口、企业买号码与合规，同一套模型卖三种人。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 三条缝：价格（开源 Fish Audio 与云厂 Polly 把低端成本压到接近零）；延迟（Cartesia 以「最快」为卖点，实时对话里延迟比音质更硬）；本地化（中文场景 MiniMax 更便宜更顺口——实测原话）。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 模型发布节奏即营销：v3、v4、Music、Dubbing 每次更新都是一次 PH 发布与媒体事件，29 次发布攒出 44K 关注。
zh.CHANNEL_2: 作品外溢：用它声音做出的播客、短视频、游戏对白，自带「这声音怎么来的」的问句。
zh.CHANNEL_3: 开发者与生态：API、MCP、集成目录；企业名单带来采购背书（Twilio、Cisco、Meta、Salesforce 等）。
zh.FRICTION_1_TITLE: 积分计费与「按月订阅」的认知冲突
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: 1 星差评的核心：页面写按月，实际按积分扣；两条 2 分钟语音扣掉 50,000 积分，客服 48 小时未回。对一个靠「多试几次才敢用」的产品，计费不透明等于把试错成本变成情绪成本。
zh.FRICTION_2_TITLE: 长文本与跨会话的声音一致性
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: 最具体的一条：长文本里数字与缩写要拼成字母才读对；跨段落、跨会话同一把声音会漂。对有声书这种「一小时不能换人」的场景这是硬伤——不是「不够像」，是「不像同一个」。
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: 评论点名中文支持弱（2 条）；实测的替代结论更直接：中文配音 MiniMax 更便宜、更符合中文习惯。中文的声调、语气词、断句与英文不是一套问题，靠通用多语种模型覆盖，会在「像外国人念中文」这一步露馅。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: 免费额度与「什么时候该付钱」说不清
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 免费 10k 积分够玩不够做；付费墙不在功能而在量，于是用户会在一次生成前突然撞墙（原话：老是触发收费），却说不清自己买的是哪一项能力。这不是价格问题，是价值刻度问题。
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方未公开运营指标。以下分两类：能核实的公开事实（价格、评论计数、模型时间线），与标注 [推断] 的「它应该看什么」，不是真实数据。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 每周被播放的生成音频时长（[推断]）
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [推断] 它按字符与分钟收费，收入随「生成后被使用」增长：只有被播出去的音频，用户才会继续生成。注册数与生成次数都会虚高——生成一次听三秒就删的人，不该算进北极星。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: 免费 → 首付的转化（第一次生成后 7 天内付费）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 免费额度刚好够验证「像不像」，付费决定发生在「我要拿它做正事」那一刻。这个窗口的转化率决定它的 PLG 效率。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: 声音留存数（克隆 + 收藏的音色）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: [推断] 存下来的声音越多，迁移成本越高。这是它最诚实的留存先行指标，比月活更接近真实黏性。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: 开发者账户的调用量与并发触顶率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: 开发者接进产品后用量会自然涨，触顶（并发 / 字符）就是升档信号。这条线决定它是「创作者工具」还是「基础设施」。
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: 版权与声音滥用的投诉数 + 生成内容的审核拦截率
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: 声音克隆是这个品类唯一可能致命的一面：未经授权克隆真人、伪造语音。它有内容审核、责任归属与出处标识，但投诉数与拦截率才是真实护栏。
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: 没有公开的留存、付费流失、单位字符推理与训练成本 [推断]
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [推断] 只看注册与评论，会看不见「免费额度越受欢迎、推理成本越重」，也看不见模型迭代（v3 → v4）的训练开销何时能摊平。
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 模型与音质 9、声音库与生态 8、品牌与发布节奏 8、开发者接口 8、企业合规 7、中文与本地化 5，加权 7：能被复制的是接口与档位，难复制的是这几年攒下的声音数据与「一耳朵就听得出」的音质。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 从人声到所有声音：音乐、音效、配音——把「声音」这一整类需求收进来。
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: 从生成到对话：ElevenAgents 接电话、接网页、接 WhatsApp，把一次性生成变成持续实时服务。
zh.VERTICAL_1: 媒体与出版：有声书、播客、视频本地化（Dubbing v2，2026-05）。
zh.VERTICAL_2: 游戏、教育、无障碍与企业客服：官网按场景切的九个入口就是它的行业地图。
zh.PLATFORM_1: 开放接口已存在：REST API、MCP 服务（api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp）、iOS 与 Android 应用。
zh.PLATFORM_2: [推断] 它的平台策略是「做所有产品的嗓子」——不争入口，争「声音这一层的默认供应商」，这也是它先做 API 再做界面的原因。
zh.OPP_1_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把中文做成第一等公民，而不是第 30 个语种
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: 怎么做：中文独立评测集（声调、语气词、断句、中英混读）+ 单独模型档与口音选项 + 价格对齐本地竞品。为什么：实测的替代结论就落在这——中文 MiniMax 更便宜、更符合中文习惯；中文是最大的内容生产市场之一，谁解决「不像外国人念中文」，谁拿走这块。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把积分翻译成用户能算的账
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: 怎么做：页面上直接把积分换算成「约多少分钟成品音频」，生成前显示本次消耗与余额，超限前给替代方案（更快的模型或更短的文本）。为什么：1 星差评的根不是贵，是算不清；实测的「老是触发收费」也是同一个病——价值刻度不清，付费就变成惊吓。
zh.OPP_3_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把声音资产做成可授权的合约层
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: 怎么做：每把克隆声音绑定用途授权（商用 / 二次分发 / 期限）与出处标识，市场上可转让可分成。为什么：它已有声音市场与 Provenance，缺的是「授权条款产品化」；做完这步，它从工具变成声音资产的基础设施，也是唯一能挡住开源免费模型的墙。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 它的赌注：用模型领先占住「像人」，用接口变成默认，用智能体把生成变成持续计费
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: 三个动作叠在一起：模型迭代保音质领先（换口碑与溢价）、API 与 MCP 把自己塞进别人的产品（换分发）、ElevenAgents 把语音从内容变成服务（换 ARPU 与续费）。最锋利的是第三个——生成是一次性的，对话是每分钟都在计费的。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 终局：任何内容都能换嗓子，任何服务都能开口
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: 如果它把声音做成像字体一样的基础设施——任何文本、任何语言、任何角色，随时可用且可授权——配音这个行业会像排版一样消失，剩下的是「声音的授权与检索」。距离不在音质（快过剩了），在两件事：授权与溯源的法律基建，以及实时对话的可靠性（电话里错一句，比录音里错一句贵得多）。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 风险按「可能性 × 影响」排序，严重度是我的判断，不是公司披露。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 模型商品化：开源与云厂追平音质
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 守住三件：情感与长文本的稳定性（开源短期难稳）、授权与溯源（企业采购的硬门槛）、实时对话的工程可靠性（延迟、并发、打断处理）。
zh.RISK_2_NAME: 声音克隆的滥用与法律风险
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 强制授权声明与本人验证、出处标识默认开启、对企业客户做 KYC 与审计日志；把「未经授权克隆」的投诉处理时限写成 SLA。
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 积分换算成「成品分钟」直接显示，生成前预估消耗，超限前提示替代方案；客服首响写进公开 SLA——1 星差评里有两条都是「没人回」。
zh.RISK_4_NAME: 中文与本地化市场的份额流失
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 中文独立模型档与口音选项，价格对齐本地竞品（实测：MiniMax 更便宜）；本地化不止语言，还有语气习惯与分发侧平台（抖音、视频号、微信读书）。

zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: ElevenAgents：电话 / 网页 / WhatsApp 的实时语音智能体，已带工作流、护栏与分析——它不只是「会说」，还能「按流程办」，是它最接近 agent 的一面。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: MCP 服务（api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp）：让 Claude、ChatGPT 直接调语音生成与智能体，等于把「开口」这一步交给外部 agent，自己只做嗓子。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [推断] 声音市场 + 克隆 + API 已经是一条「供给 → 授权 → 分发」链，只差「替人接活」的授权；补上之后，它从内容工具变成声音劳动的外包层。
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: 两条：一是音质本身在商品化（开源与云厂追平），溢价只能靠品牌与生态维持；二是「配音 / 播音」这类岗位被直接压掉——它自己就是那把刀，所以风险在需求侧被替代后价格随之下探。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）中文与多语种的情感控制，是它最该补、也最能拉开差距的一层。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把声音做成可授权、可溯源、可分成的资产层——从生成音频延伸到交易与治理，这是唯一能抬客单价又不冒犯创作者的方向。
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 可核实：官网与文档的功能清单、三块产品线、90+ 语言与 17,500 声音、模型时间线与版本日期、定价六档金额与积分、并发与音色槽位对照、企业客户名单、Provenance 与内容审核、PH 4.9 / 236 与评论计数。未核实 / 不引用：G2 分数（本次抓取失败）、竞品定价原文（未逐一读取）、官方 ARR 与用户数（未披露）。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: [推断] 积分与字符的换算随模型档位不同而异（v3 / v4 比 Flash 贵），定价页只给「额外一分钟约 $0.36 → $0.17」这种区间，任何按积分反推的 ARR 都不可信。
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: [推断] 付费主力是创作者档（$22）与开发者用量，而非企业；依据是 PH 评论里创作者口吻占多数、定价页把 Creator 放在推荐位，官方未披露结构。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 它站在两条货架的交叉口：一边是语音合成（云厂 TTS、开源模型），一边是语音智能体（Vapi 这类编排层）。位置上它两边都做，并用同一套模型供给三种人——创作者买界面，开发者买接口，企业买号码与合规。好处是没有单一对手能整块压过来；坏处是每条线都有一个更强的专才。
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 出现在六处：TTS（多模型档）、声音克隆（少量样本复刻音色）、STT（Scribe 系列，含实时）、配音（整段音视频换语言并保留音色）、音乐与音效生成、语音智能体（实时对话、工具调用、护栏、分析）。对外还有 API 与 MCP，让别的 AI 直接调这些能力。
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 要绝对稳定同一把声音的长篇有声书（评论：长文本会漂）；中文为主且预算敏感的项目（实测：MiniMax 更便宜更合适）；需要私有化部署、数据不出内网的行业；要求零 AI 痕迹且不接受任何标识的场景。
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 护城河「中偏强」，强在模型与生态，不强在锁定：音质领先（可被追平但需要时间）、17,500 声音库与声音市场（网络效应偏弱）、API 与 MCP 的分发（接入后替换要排期）、企业名单背书。真正薄的一环是中文与本地化——那里它只是「多语种之一」。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 音质与情感的自然度、克隆的可用性、三种交付形态（界面 / 接口 / 智能体）、出处标识与合规先行、企业客户名单。
zh.SIX_INTRO: 按应用层六个维度写：不看它有多少模型，看它替掉了哪一步、又把什么麻烦甩回来。证据：2026-11-20 的 20 分钟实测（燃冰）、官网与定价页原文、Product Hunt 抓到的评论计数与原话方向。
zh.AI_TYPE_REASON: 拔电测试：拿走 TTS 与克隆模型，剩下的只有编辑器、声音库、接口与计费——没有模型，它连一段音频都生不出来，所以判为原生（AI-native）。而且是「整机原生」：产品本身就是模型的直译，不像会议工具那样有「记录壳 + AI 脑」的两段式。
zh.SIX_1: 替掉「开口录」这一步：原来要自己念或约配音，改一个字就得重录；现在录一段就能复用到不同场景（实测原话：原来是直接说 / 录，现在提取声音覆盖不同场景）。成本从录音棚工时变成 10k 免费额度 + $6 起。
zh.SIX_2: 它啃掉配音、多语种、多角色、音效与配乐；甩回两件：录一段干净的声音样本（克隆要样本）、选声音与调参——而选声音本来就得人做（实测原话：脏活不用手动补，本来就得做的是录声音、选声音）。它更像声音组件库：零件它给，组装还是你。
zh.SIX_3: 能直接用，但要改就得付钱（实测原话：可以直接用，也提供修改机会但要收费）；要改的往往是「性格」——录了自己的声音，听着却不像自己。对外单发没意义，它的产出是素材不是成品（用于有声书、视频、个人分身）。
zh.SIX_4: 兜底有三层但都不在内容上：出处标识能判断一段音频是否 AI 生成（实测评价：挺好）、内容审核、以及积分本身形成的刹车。但实测的判断是「没有兜底机制」——它不校验你念的内容对不对，错的话照样读得很好听。
zh.SIX_5: 错得起。每次生成都消耗积分（错了要重花），支持实时声音转换，改稿成本低（实测原话：错得起）。真正贵的一次是把不像自己的声音发出去——那是声誉成本，产品兜不了。
zh.SIX_6: 换得掉。实测原话：其他声音模型可以替代，中文用 MiniMax 更好更便宜；结论是「模型它最好，但换得掉」。做产品的人换的成本在接口与调参，创作者换的成本在一把新声音要重新养。

en.CATEGORY: AI voice generation / voice agents (ai-voice-agents · text-to-speech)
en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It does not sell dubbing - it sells a voice that can be copied, edited and dropped into any context. Audio quality is the wall; the credit system is the gate people complain about most.
en.USER_SCALE: Verifiable: the site claims 90+ languages and 17,500+ voices; Product Hunt shows 4.9 / 236 reviews / 44K followers / 29 launches (listed 2023); the Enterprise logo wall verifiably includes Twilio, Disney, Stripe, Cisco, NVIDIA, Meta, Zoom, Klarna, Salesforce, Adobe, IBM and Deutsche Telekom. Caveat: the PH tagline says 70+ languages while the site says 90+, so each is quoted as written. The G2 scrape failed this round, so no G2 score is cited. ARR, user count and paying customers are not disclosed and are not invented here.
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Mature. The product is split three ways: ElevenCreative (TTS, voice cloning, dubbing, music, sound effects, plus image and video tools), ElevenAgents (voice agents for phone, web and WhatsApp with testing, guardrails, workflows and analytics) and ElevenAPI (speech, music, sound effects, dubbing and transcription APIs, including an MCP server). The model line runs from Multilingual v2 in Aug 2023 to Eleven v4 in Sep 2026, via Turbo v2, Flash v2.5, the Scribe transcription series, Music v2 and Dubbing v2 (May 2026).
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Credit-based subscriptions + enterprise contracts + startup programme. Six tiers: Free $0 (10k credits/month), Starter $1 first month then $6 (30k), Creator $11 first month then $22 (121k, the recommended slot), Pro $99 (600k), Scale $299 (1.8M, 3 seats), Business $990 (6M, 10 seats), Enterprise on request; annual plans up to 55% off for Black Friday; startups get 12 months free and 33M characters.
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It is the model layer for voice turned into a component library plus a socket: voices can be cloned, reused and billed per character. The wall is not the feature list - it is the last mile of sounding human, and the fact that Chinese users have cheaper options.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: The pull-the-plug test says AI-native: remove the voice models and only the editor, the voice library, the API and the billing remain - the product instantly becomes a shell. So the moat sits on both sides: the model side is fidelity of timbre, emotion and prosody; the price side is credits converted into minutes, cheaper as you go but prepaid. The hand test (RanBing) puts it best in one line: it feels like a voice component library - the more complete the parts, the clearer it is that it sells parts, not finished goods.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: Audio quality is the one thing you cannot substitute
en.TLDR_1_BODY: The three things reviewers praise most point at the same spot: naturalness (60 mentions), believable cloning (22) and language coverage (15). The most concrete complaint points at it too: across long texts and sessions the same voice drifts, and numbers and abbreviations must be spelled out letter by letter. Users pay for sounding alike and leave the moment it stops sounding like the same person.
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: The moat is the model, not the interface
en.TLDR_2_BODY: Three questions from the hand test: worth the price - yes, because a voice can be copied and even traded in the voice marketplace; is the barrier the model or something else - the model and the accumulated voice data, not the interaction design. The UI only exists so you can paste a script; what decides the outcome is how the model handles emotion, accent and long sentences. Same conclusion as 010 Fathom (the barrier is recognition): for AI products the wall sits on the model side.
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: Three weak beams: credit billing, Chinese localisation, open source and hyperscalers catching up
en.TLDR_3_BODY: First: 1-star reviews cluster on credits - the page says monthly, the meter deducts credits, two 2-minute clips burned 50,000 credits, support went silent for 48 hours. Second: Chinese needs a workaround (the hand test: MiniMax is cheaper and more idiomatic for Chinese dubbing). Third: Deepgram, Cartesia Sonic and Fish Audio sit in the same rack, the gap is narrowing and prices keep falling.
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: ElevenLabs is an AI voice company: text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing, music and transcription models turn text into a reusable human voice, delivered three ways - a web studio for creators (ElevenCreative), voice agents for enterprises (ElevenAgents) and an API for developers (ElevenAPI, including an MCP server).
en.USER_PROMISE: Official line (PH tagline verbatim): Create natural AI voices instantly in any language. In user language: paste a script and seconds later you get a voice you can ship, in any licensed timbre and any language.
en.SEGMENT_1_NAME: Individual creators (podcasts, audiobooks, short video, narration)
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: Previously you recorded yourself or hired a voice actor, and one edit meant a re-record. The hand test (RanBing) lands in this layer and judges the product as aimed mainly at creators: 10k free credits are enough to try, the recommended tier is $22. Reviews are densest here too: plan, script, recording and post collapse into one step, and two days of work become half a day.
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: They do not buy the UI, they buy the interface: speech, transcription, dubbing, music and agent APIs plus an MCP endpoint (api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp). API integration is mentioned 14 times in reviews and is a main reason people pick it; this layer buys latency (Flash at 75ms) and concurrency (10 to 6000 by tier).
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: They check three things: compliance (content moderation, responsibility, Provenance detection of AI-generated audio), whether voice agents can answer phones and WhatsApp, and the procurement comfort of a big-logo customer list (Twilio, Disney, Stripe, Cisco, NVIDIA, Meta, Zoom, Salesforce, Adobe and others on the site).
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Turn a script into a shippable voice, and swap the person, the language or the emotion without re-recording.
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Edit the copy without another take - never read the same sentence into a microphone for the fifth time.
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: The work sounds like it came from a team with a budget; one person can ship something that has a voice.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: One word in the script changes and the whole segment must be re-recorded; or a multi-language version is needed and you only speak Chinese.
en.FREQUENCY: It follows content production rhythm: a few times a week to daily for creators; agent scenarios run 24/7 ([inferred] because Agents are billed by concurrency and minutes; call frequency is not disclosed).
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Paste, pick a voice, tune parameters and export in the web studio; developers call the API inside their own products; enterprises wire voices into phone support, game dialogue, video localisation and audiobook pipelines.
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: The trigger is not I want to use AI but this copy needs to become audio and I do not want to record it - the marginal cost of recording is your throat.
en.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: Paste, pick a voice, tune, generate
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: The hand-test path: understand the pitch on the landing page, enter the studio, pick a library voice or clone your own, paste and generate. The friction is concrete: errors inside the flow, and paywalls appearing right before the key action (verbatim note: it kept triggering charges).
en.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: Seconds later you have audio you can ship
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: Hand-test verdict: usable as is, but changes cost money. What needs changing is usually personality - you clone your own voice and the output does not sound like you.
en.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: The voice is stored, so next time nothing is re-configured
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: People return not to generate once more but because my voice, my projects and my past scripts live here. Clone once and reuse forever: that is the real retention mechanism and the line between it and one-off dubbing outsourcing.
en.LOOP_FREQ: Content cadence: 3-10 times a week ([inferred] from creator publishing rhythm and the 10k/month free allowance; not disclosed).
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The same action keeps recurring: once the script is locked it needs a voice. The loop compresses book a booth, record, edit into paste, pick, export.
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What it really teaches users is that a voice can be an asset - after one use people start raising a different voice for each show instead of hunting for a voice actor every time.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Three loops run at once: word of mouth through the output (content made with its voices carries the question where did that voice come from), release cadence (29 launches, 44K followers, every new model is an event) and the developer ecosystem plus integration directories (API, MCP, and it is always named when users discuss alternatives).
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: The first time you hear your own voice speaking another language - cloning stacked on multilingual. The hand test did not time it, but the first recorded reaction was: I can extract my voice and cover different scenarios.
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Yes, but as output-borne virality: the audio is heard in podcasts, short video and games, and listeners ask who voiced it. It is not link-sharing virality (generations do not carry a built-in share funnel); conversion from sharing is not disclosed [inferred].
en.RETENTION_1: Cloned voices and past projects pile up in the account, so leaving means rebuilding the voice assets.
en.RETENTION_2: Once a team workspace or API key is wired into a product, switching means code changes and re-tuning, not a few clicks.
en.RETENTION_3: Model iterations make old voices sound better - the same voice regenerated on v3 or v4 is more natural, giving users a reason to redo old content ([inferred] from the public model timeline and upgrade posts).
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: New model (v3 to v4, Music v2, Dubbing v2) brings existing users back to redo work, the output spreads, new users try it, the 10k free allowance runs out and they convert. This loop is only as strong as the audible difference in each upgrade.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: A developer ships one small TTS feature, usage grows, concurrency and character limits bite, they upgrade or negotiate enterprise terms. Once embedded it is infrastructure, and the switching cost moves from I do not like it to I would have to schedule it.
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: The main door. Paste, pick a voice, tune stability and similarity, generate, export; the model tier (v3 / v4 / Flash / Turbo) decides latency and naturalness. This is also where the hand test kept hitting paywalls.
en.SURFACE_2_NAME: Voice cloning and the voice library
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: Where the moat sits. 17,500+ voices are usable directly and cloning turns your own voice into a reusable asset; the component-library comment from the hand test refers to this layer.
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Swaps the language of a whole audio or video while keeping the original speaker's timbre and pacing; Dubbing v2 shipped in May 2026. It sells going global without re-recording.
en.SURFACE_4_NAME: Music and sound effects (Eleven Music / SFX)
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: Extends from voices to all sound: score and effects, Music launched Aug 2025 and Music v2 in May 2026. For creators it saves a licensing fee; for the company it lifts ARPU.
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: From generating content to real-time conversation: phone, web and WhatsApp, with testing, guardrails, workflows and analytics. This layer bills minutes and concurrency and is how a creator tool becomes business infrastructure.
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: Money and lock-in both live here: per-character and per-minute billing, concurrency and seats by tier, and MCP so Claude and ChatGPT can call it directly. The pricing page's voice slots (3 / 10 / 30 / 160 / 660 / 2200) say more about commercial intent than the feature table.
en.ENTITY_1: Voice (a reusable voice, cloned or picked from the library)
en.ENTITY_2: Project / Generation (one render, replayable and exportable)
en.ENTITY_3: Credit (the unit of money, derived from characters and minutes)
en.ENTITY_4: Agent (a voice agent that can answer a phone)
en.ENTITY_5: Workspace / Seat (the boundary for team, concurrency and permissions)
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: The spine is the voice: a library voice or your clone goes into a project, the project produces generations, and generations split by use (video, audiobook, game, phone). The upside is compounding - the more voices you store, the more it is worth; the cost is that the product has no natural ending, so users stop at generation and assemble the goods elsewhere.
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Hand-test path (RanBing): the landing page explains the scenarios (games, conversational, narration, characters, education and so on), then the studio, then pick or clone a voice, then paste and generate. Learning cost is low; the blockers are two - occasional errors mid-flow and constant paywalls (verbatim: it kept triggering charges).
en.CRAFT_1_NAME: A survey-style entry priced by use case
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: Pricing first asks what you want to do (creator, podcast and audiobook, marketing, film and TV, music and SFX, games, education and accessibility, dubbing, personal), then shows tiers. The hand test noticed exactly this: it does not let you compare prices, it makes you claim a scenario first, swapping is it expensive for is it enough.
en.CRAFT_2_NAME: Turning does it sound like me into two dials
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Separating stability from similarity is the most practical design in this category: want consistency across long text and accept some drift, or want likeness and accept occasional wobble. The hand-test complaint (it does not sound like me) is really these two dials set wrong, and the product leaves the solving to the user.
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: It can tell whether a piece of audio was AI-generated. The hand-test reaction was this is good - marking your own output in a category that will be abused is an investment in long-term trust and an entry ticket for enterprise procurement.
en.CRAFT_4_NAME: A genuinely usable free tier, then quantity gates
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: 10k free credits a month is just enough to validate a few clips; daily publishing inevitably hits the wall. The wall is quantity, not features (features are basically open) - so the trial is complete but when should I pay becomes blurry, and that is exactly where the 1-star credit confusion grows.
en.CRAFT_5_NAME: A voice marketplace that turns users into supply
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: The hand test noted this detail: a tradeable voice marketplace exists and creators can earn there. The point is not the commission but outsourcing voice supply to users, turning a tool into an exchange ([inferred] network effects depend on revenue share and licensing terms, which are not published).
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Perfect sounding human first, workflows second. Every craft choice reduces the moment where you can tell it is AI, rather than adding another button.
en.TTV_LABEL: Time to value: not measured this round (the hand test logged only the sequence - understand the scenario, open the studio, pick a voice, paste, get audio - with no stopwatch)
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: The hand test recorded outcomes, not seconds. This report does not convert it into minutes and does not invent scores.
en.COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: low (the studio is direct - paste and it renders; the hard part is which dial to turn, not where to click)
en.DELIGHT_1: Clone once, reuse for good: record your own voice and every later script can use it.
en.DELIGHT_2: One person does the work of a voice team: multi-language, multi-character, multi-emotion without booking a booth.
en.DELIGHT_3: Provenance and content moderation are in place - it does not pretend not to see (hand-test verdict: this is good).
en.DELIGHT_LABEL: Delight: voices as assets, multi-language on demand, deliberate AI marking
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: 4.9 across 236 reviews on the product side, content moderation, responsibility and provenance on the compliance side; the weak spot is billing transparency - a 1-star review says the page quotes monthly while the meter deducts credits, with 48 hours of silence from support.
en.STRUGGLE_1: Billing confusion: priced monthly, deducted in credits; two 2-minute clips cost 50,000 credits (direction of the 1-star review).
en.STRUGGLE_2: Consistency across long text and sessions: the same voice drifts between paragraphs and sessions; numbers and abbreviations must be spelled out (review cons).
en.STRUGGLE_3: Chinese and accents: weak Chinese support is named twice; the hand-test substitute was MiniMax (cheaper, more idiomatic Chinese).
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Friction: credit billing, long-text consistency, Chinese and accents
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Six self-serve tiers ($0 / 6 / 22 / 99 / 299 / 990, Starter $1 first month, Creator $11 first month) plus enterprise contracts; unit price falls with tier (about $0.36 to $0.17 per extra minute), voice slots 3 to 2200, concurrency 10 to 6000.
en.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: Entry as cheap as one dollar, money collected on usage and enterprise
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: Starter at $1 and Creator at $11 turn try into subscribe; the real money is in usage above Pro, in seats and concurrency at Scale and Business, and in enterprise contracts. Credit billing lets revenue grow with usage - and makes running out a routine complaint.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free: 10k credits per month, library voices available, cloning capped, commercial use licensed by tier. Paid: more credits, more voice slots, higher concurrency, 192kbps fidelity, commercial licence, teams and priority support. The wall is not features - it is volume and licensing.
en.UX_MON_HEADLINE: Are experience and monetisation aligned, or fighting?
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Half aligned. Aligned: generation takes zero learning, the free allowance is just enough to hear that it sounds human, and the paywall lands on volume, concurrency and licensing - things you only miss once you use it for real. Fighting: every advanced action (change personality, regenerate, export high quality) sits behind payment, and the hand test felt it as constant charging prompts - smoothness and restraint pull in opposite directions here.

en.COMP_OWN_D2: In-house TTS / STT / music / dubbing models + cloning + 17,500-voice library + agent orchestration + API / MCP

Competitor pricing pages were not read one by one, so no unread price is written.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Two gaps that are hard to close short term: audio quality and emotional performance (praise clusters on naturalness and believable cloning - a model and data gap); and three delivery shapes existing at once - creators buy the UI, developers buy the API, enterprises buy numbers and compliance, all from one set of models.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Three seams: price (open-source Fish Audio and Polly push the low end toward zero); latency (Cartesia sells fastest, and in real-time conversation latency is harder than quality); localisation (MiniMax is cheaper and smoother for Chinese - hand-test words).
en.CHANNEL_1: Release cadence as marketing: v3, v4, Music, Dubbing - every update is a PH launch and a media event, 29 launches accumulating 44K followers.
en.CHANNEL_2: Output-borne spread: podcasts, short video and game dialogue made with these voices carry the question of where the voice came from.
en.CHANNEL_3: Developers and ecosystem: API, MCP, integration directories; the enterprise logo wall supplies procurement credibility (Twilio, Cisco, Meta, Salesforce and others).
en.FRICTION_1_TITLE: Credit billing versus the monthly subscription mental model
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: The core of the 1-star review: the page says monthly, the meter deducts credits, two 2-minute clips burn 50,000 credits, and support goes quiet for 48 hours. For a product that needs several tries before you dare use it, opaque billing turns trial cost into emotional cost.
en.FRICTION_2_TITLE: Voice consistency across long text and sessions
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: The most concrete complaint: in long texts numbers and abbreviations must be spelled out letter by letter, and the same voice drifts across paragraphs and sessions. For audiobooks - an hour where the speaker cannot change - that is fatal: it is not not similar enough, it is not the same person.
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: Reviews name weak Chinese support (2 mentions); the hand test is blunter: for Chinese dubbing MiniMax is cheaper and more idiomatic. Chinese tones, particles, phrasing and mixed Chinese-English reading are a different problem set; covering them with a general multilingual model shows up exactly at sounds like a foreigner reading Chinese.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Free allowance versus when should I pay
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: 10k free credits are enough to play and not enough to work; the wall is quantity, not features, so users hit it right before a generation (verbatim: it kept triggering charges) without being able to say which capability they bought. That is not a pricing problem, it is a value-scale problem.
en.METRICS_INTRO: No operating metrics are disclosed. What follows splits in two: public facts that can be verified (prices, review counts, model timeline) and what it should be watching, marked [inferred], not real data.
en.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: Weekly hours of generated audio that actually get played ([inferred])
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [inferred] It bills per character and per minute, so revenue grows with being used after generation: only audio that gets heard makes users generate again. Sign-ups and generation counts both inflate - someone who generates once, listens for three seconds and deletes should not count toward the north star.
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: Free-to-first-payment conversion (paying within 7 days of the first generation)
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: The free allowance is just enough to test whether it sounds human; the payment decision happens at the moment of I want to use this for real work. Conversion inside that window decides how efficient its PLG is.
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: [inferred] The more voices stored, the higher the switching cost. It is the most honest leading retention indicator, closer to real stickiness than MAU.
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: Developer account volume and rate of hitting the concurrency ceiling
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: Once a developer embeds it, usage grows naturally; hitting the ceiling (concurrency or characters) is the upgrade signal. This line decides whether it is a creator tool or infrastructure.
en.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: Copyright and voice-abuse complaints plus moderation interception rate
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Voice cloning is the one potentially fatal face of this category: cloning a real person without authority, faking speech. It has content moderation, responsibility and provenance marking, but complaints and interception rates are the real guardrail.
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: No public retention, churn, unit inference cost or training cost [inferred]
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [inferred] Watching only sign-ups and reviews hides that the more popular the free allowance, the heavier the inference cost - and hides when model iterations (v3 to v4) can amortise their training spend.
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Model and audio quality 9, voice library and ecosystem 8, brand and release cadence 8, developer APIs 8, enterprise compliance 7, Chinese and localisation 5, weighted to 7: the interfaces and tiers are copyable, the years of voice data and the instantly audible quality are not.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: From human voices to all sound: music, effects, dubbing - absorbing the whole sound category.
en.HORIZONTAL_2: From generation to conversation: ElevenAgents answers phones, web and WhatsApp, turning one-off renders into continuous real-time service.
en.VERTICAL_1: Media and publishing: audiobooks, podcasts, video localisation (Dubbing v2, May 2026).
en.VERTICAL_2: Games, education, accessibility and enterprise support: the nine use-case entries on the site are its industry map.
en.PLATFORM_1: Open interfaces already exist: REST API, MCP server (api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp), iOS and Android apps.
en.PLATFORM_2: [inferred] Its platform strategy is to be the vocal cords of every product - not fighting for the entry point but for being the default voice layer, which is why the API came before the UI.
en.OPP_1_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Make Chinese a first-class citizen, not language number thirty
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How: an independent Chinese evaluation set (tones, particles, phrasing, mixed Chinese-English reading), a dedicated model tier and accent options, and pricing aligned with local rivals. Why: the hand test's substitution decision lands exactly here - MiniMax is cheaper and more idiomatic for Chinese; Chinese is one of the largest content-production markets, and whoever fixes sounds like a foreigner reading Chinese takes it.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Translate credits into arithmetic users can do
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: How: show on the page how many finished minutes a credit balance buys, display the cost and remaining balance before generating, and offer alternatives near the limit (faster model, shorter text). Why: the root of the 1-star review is not price but arithmetic - and the hand test's constant charging prompts are the same disease: when the value scale is unclear, paying feels like a shock.
en.OPP_3_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Turn voice assets into a licensable contract layer
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: How: bind every cloned voice to usage rights (commercial, redistribution, term) and provenance, transferable and rev-shared in the marketplace. Why: the marketplace and provenance already exist; what is missing is productising the licence - do that and it moves from tool to voice-asset infrastructure, the only wall that holds against free open-source models.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: Its bet: hold sounding human with model lead, become the default through APIs, turn generation into continuous billing with agents
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: Three moves stacked: model iteration keeps quality leadership (buys reputation and premium), API and MCP insert it into other products (buys distribution), and ElevenAgents turns voice from content into service (buys ARPU and renewals). The sharpest is the third - generation is one-off, conversation bills every minute.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Endgame: any content can change voices, any service can speak
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: If a voice becomes infrastructure like a typeface - any text, any language, any character, available and licensable on demand - dubbing as an industry disappears the way typesetting did, leaving licensing and retrieval of voices. The distance is not audio quality (nearly surplus), it is two things: legal infrastructure for licensing and provenance, and reliability of real-time conversation (one wrong sentence on a call costs far more than one wrong sentence in a recording).
en.RISK_INTRO: Risks are ordered by likelihood times impact; severity is my judgement, not company disclosure.
en.RISK_1_NAME: Model commoditisation: open source and hyperscalers catch up on quality
en.RISK_1_MIT: Hold three things: emotional and long-text stability (hard for open source to stabilise short term), licensing and provenance (hard gates for enterprise procurement) and engineering reliability of real-time conversation (latency, concurrency, interruption handling).
en.RISK_2_MIT: Mandatory consent statements and speaker verification, provenance on by default, KYC and audit logs for enterprise customers, and a published SLA for handling unauthorised-clone complaints.
en.RISK_3_MIT: Show credits translated into finished minutes, estimate cost before generating, offer alternatives before the limit, and publish a first-response SLA - two of the 1-star complaints were nobody answered.
en.RISK_4_NAME: Losing share in Chinese and localised markets
en.RISK_4_MIT: A dedicated Chinese model tier and accent options, with pricing aligned to local rivals (hand test: MiniMax is cheaper); localisation is not only language but phrasing habits and distribution channels (Douyin, WeChat Channels, WeRead).

en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: ElevenAgents: real-time voice agents on phone, web and WhatsApp, already carrying workflows, guardrails and analytics - it does not just talk, it follows a process, which is its most agent-like face.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: The MCP server (api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp) lets Claude and ChatGPT call voice generation and agents directly, handing the speaking step to an external agent while it supplies the voice.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [inferred] Marketplace, cloning and API already form a supply, licence, distribution chain; the only missing piece is authority to take work on someone's behalf - add that and it becomes an outsourcing layer for voice labour.
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: Two: audio quality itself is commoditising (open source and hyperscalers catching up), so the premium can only be defended by brand and ecosystem; and voice-over and announcing jobs are being compressed away - it is the knife itself, so the risk is demand-side substitution pulling prices down.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (my judgement) Emotional control in Chinese and other languages is the layer it most needs and could widen the gap with.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (my judgement) Turn voices into licensable, traceable, rev-shared assets - extending from generating audio into trading and governing it, the only direction that raises ARPU without offending creators.
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Verifiable: feature lists on site and docs, the three product lines, 90+ languages and 17,500 voices, the model timeline and version dates, six pricing tiers with credits, concurrency and voice-slot comparisons, the enterprise logo wall, provenance and moderation, and PH 4.9 / 236 with review counts. Not verified / not cited: the G2 score (scrape failed), competitor pricing pages (not read one by one), official ARR and user numbers (not disclosed).
en.ASSUMPTION_1: [inferred] The credit-to-character ratio differs by model tier (v3 / v4 cost more than Flash); the pricing page only gives a range of about $0.36 to $0.17 per extra minute, so any ARR back-calculated from credits is unreliable.
en.ASSUMPTION_2: [inferred] The paying base is mainly creator tier ($22) plus developer usage rather than enterprise; the basis is creator-toned voices dominating PH reviews and Creator sitting in the recommended slot, with no disclosed revenue mix.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: It stands where two shelves intersect: speech synthesis (hyperscaler TTS, open models) and voice agents (orchestration layers such as Vapi). It does both and feeds three kinds of buyer from one set of models - creators buy the UI, developers buy the API, enterprises buy numbers and compliance. The upside is that no single rival can press on the whole block; the downside is that every line has a stronger specialist.
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI appears in six places: TTS (multiple model tiers), voice cloning (a few samples reproducing a timbre), STT (the Scribe series, including streaming), dubbing (whole audio or video re-voiced while keeping timbre), music and sound-effect generation, and voice agents (real-time conversation, tool calls, guardrails, analytics). Externally there are APIs and MCP so other AI can call these capabilities directly.
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Long audiobooks that need one absolutely stable voice (reviews: it drifts on long text); Chinese-first projects on a budget (hand test: MiniMax is cheaper and better suited); industries requiring private deployment with data kept on-premise; scenarios demanding zero AI traces and no marking at all.
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: The moat is medium-to-strong: strong on models and ecosystem, weak on lock-in. Quality lead (closable but time-consuming), a 17,500-voice library and marketplace (weak network effects), API and MCP distribution (switching requires scheduling), enterprise logos. The genuinely thin part is Chinese and localisation - there it is just one of many languages.
en.FINAL_WINS: Audio quality and emotional naturalness, usable cloning, three delivery shapes (UI / API / agents), provenance and compliance ahead of the field, and an enterprise logo wall.
en.SIX_INTRO: Written against the six application-layer dimensions: not how many models it has, but which step it replaces and what trouble it hands back. Evidence: the 20-minute hand test on 2026-11-20 (RanBing), the site and pricing page copy, and the review counts and tone captured from Product Hunt.
en.AI_TYPE_REASON: Pull-the-plug test: remove the TTS and cloning models and only the editor, the voice library, the API and billing remain - without the models it cannot produce a single second of audio, so it is AI-native. And native all the way through: the product is a direct rendering of the model, unlike meeting tools that are a recording shell plus an AI brain.
en.SIX_1: It replaces the step of opening your mouth to record: previously you read it yourself or hired a voice actor and one changed word meant re-recording; now one recording is reused across scenarios (hand-test words: previously you just spoke or recorded, now you extract the voice and cover different scenarios). Cost moves from studio hours to 10k free credits plus $6.
en.SIX_2: It swallows dubbing, multi-language, multi-character, effects and score; it hands back two things: a clean recording of your voice (cloning needs samples) and picking a voice plus tuning - and picking a voice was always human work (hand-test words: the dirty work needs no manual patching; what you always had to do is record a voice and choose one). It is more like a voice component library: parts supplied, assembly still yours.
en.SIX_3: Usable as is, but changes cost money (hand-test words: usable directly, and it offers revisions for a fee); what needs changing is usually personality - you clone your own voice and hear someone else. Single-shot output is not a finished product; its output is material (for audiobooks, video, personal avatars).
en.SIX_4: There are three safety nets, none of them about content: provenance can tell whether audio is AI-generated (hand-test verdict: good), content moderation exists, and credits act as a brake. But the hand-test conclusion is that there is no safety net - it does not check whether what you wrote is right, and wrong text is read out beautifully.
en.SIX_5: Errors are affordable. Each generation burns credits (redo means paying again), real-time voice conversion is supported and revisions are cheap (hand-test words: errors are affordable). The expensive error is shipping a voice that does not sound like you - a reputation cost the product cannot absorb.
en.SIX_6: Substitutable. Hand-test words: other voice models can replace it, and for Chinese MiniMax is better and cheaper; the conclusion is its model is the best, but it can be swapped. For builders the switching cost is API and tuning; for creators it is raising a new voice from scratch.

extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
缺件先说：Product Hunt 产品页正文受 Cloudflare 限制，只拿到元数据（4.9 / 236 / 44K 关注）与评论计数，没拿到 More alternatives 栏目；竞品定价页本次也未逐一读取。所以这张地图的名单不来自「顺手抓取」，而来自三处——PH 的 Similar Products、评论里用户自己说的替代、以及实测（燃冰）点的中文替代。

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
Deepgram要 ASR 与语音接口的开发者转写 + 语音接口（TTS 为补位）它的邻居而非对手：一个把语音转成字，一个把字转成语音；PH 4.9 分 86 条，开发者口碑扎实
Cartesia（Sonic）要低延迟实时语音的开发者实时 TTS 与语音对话最直接的性能对手：以「最快」为卖点，实时对话里延迟比音质更硬；PH 5.0 分 25 条
Fish Audio想便宜、想自托管的声音克隆用户开源 TTS + 克隆 + 托管价格侧最狠的一刀：开源免费可自部署，PH 4.7 分 15 条
Vapi想快速搭语音 agent 的团队智能体编排层（可接各家 TTS）抢的是「入口」而不是「嗓子」：它把你的模型当零件用，PH 4.9 分 25 条
Rask AI要视频本地化的团队配音 + 字幕 + 多语种分发抢 Dubbing 这一层，PH 4.8 分 28 条；对它是「单点更专」的对手
云厂 TTS（Polly / Google Cloud）已在云上的企业通用 TTS，按字符计费评论里被点名的替代：稳定、便宜、不用新签一家供应商，但不追求「像人」

结论：它的位置特殊——既被当「零件」卖给别人（Vapi 这类编排层接它的模型），又要自己卖「整机」（Agents）。这决定了它的对手不只是同类，还包括「把它当零件」的平台。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
这一段只写能站住的：自家底座按官网与文档原文，别人的底座按 PH 一句话与公开定位；具体毫秒数、参数量、价格一律不猜。

  • ElevenLabs：自研 TTS / STT / 音乐 / 配音模型 + 声音库 + 智能体编排 + API / MCP。接缝在「模型换代」：每换一版（v3 → v4），旧内容要重生成才好听，这既是黏性也是成本。
  • Deepgram：ASR 起家的语音平台，转写是主场、TTS 是补位；优势在接口的成熟度与开发者信任。
  • Cartesia：自研实时语音模型，一切围绕延迟；[推断] 这类底座在电话客服、实时对话里比「更自然」更能决定体验。
  • Fish Audio：开源 TTS + 托管，用户可自己部署；护城河反过来压在自己身上——价格被开源锚定。
  • 云厂 TTS：长在既有账单与目录里，零获客成本；技术上不追「像人」，追可用性与合规。

[推断] 这个品类真正的护城河不在「能不能生成」，在「一把声音跨文本、跨语言、跨会话还是同一个人」——靠的是数据与评测体系，不是参数量。这也解释了为什么评论里最具体的抱怨全是「不一致」。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会（我的判断）
extra_zh.body:
四条，按「能不能一个人做」排序，不是按想象力排序。

  1. 把积分翻译成「成品分钟」：页面上直接显示「这次生成约几十分钟音频、余额还能做几条」，超限前给替代方案（更快的模型 / 更短的文本）。最轻——纯产品文案与预估逻辑，一个人一周能做完。
  2. 中文独立模型档：声调、语气词、断句、中英混读单独评测与调优，口音可选项，价格对齐本地竞品。最值——中文是最大的内容生产市场之一，而现在的通用多语种模型会在「像外国人念中文」这一步露馅。
  3. 授权条款产品化：每把克隆声音绑定用途授权（商用 / 二次分发 / 期限）与出处标识，市场上可转让可分成。最重，但也最难被开源免费追平。
  4. 「粘贴即预览」的配音闭环：把配音与对口型 / 剪辑串起来，别让用户拿着素材去别处拼。这是把「素材」变「成品」的那一步，也是它现在最明显的产品断点。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
钱从三层人的兜里出，窗口在收窄。

钱从谁的兜里出：原本付给配音员、录音棚、本地化公司的预算——本质是替掉「人声这份工时」。创作者每月 $22 换的是「不用约棚」，企业年框换的是「不用招人」。

还能拿多久：窗口在收窄。开源 TTS 与云厂 TTS 正在把「能生成」变成免费默认，溢价只能压在「像人」的最后那段与生态上。它自己的应对是把重心往 Agents 移——从按字符卖内容，转到按分钟卖服务。

凭什么你拿到：模型代际领先 + 29 次发布攒的关注 + API / MCP 变成别人的默认嗓子 + 企业名单背书。四件事缺一件，价格就守不住。

流量吃三段：作品外溢（用它的声音做出来的内容自带问句）、模型发布（每次新版即 PH 与媒体事件）、开发者目录（API、MCP、云市场）。变现三层：订阅（广度）→ 用量与并发（厚度）→ 企业年框与合规（深度）。

最脆的梁：积分制与「按月」的认知落差——1 星差评全在这儿；再叠一层：中文一侧它只是「多语种之一」，本地竞品更便宜更顺口。

extra_en.title: Competitive map
extra_en.body:
Missing piece first: the Product Hunt body was blocked by Cloudflare, so we have metadata (4.9 / 236 / 44K followers) and review counts but no More alternatives section, and competitor pricing pages were not read one by one. So this map is not a by-product of scraping - names come from three places: PH Similar Products, substitutes users name in reviews, and the Chinese alternatives noted in the hand test (RanBing).

WhoFights for the same needFights on the same linkWhere users actually move
DeepgramDevelopers needing ASR and speech APIsTranscription plus speech APIs (TTS as a follow-on)A neighbour, not a rival: one turns speech into text, the other text into speech; 4.9 across 86 PH reviews, solid developer reputation
Cartesia (Sonic)Developers needing low-latency real-time speechReal-time TTS and spoken conversationThe most direct performance rival, selling fastest; in real-time conversation latency is harder than quality; 5.0 across 25 reviews
Fish AudioVoice-cloning users who want cheap and self-hostedOpen-source TTS plus cloning plus hostingThe hardest cut on price: open source, free, self-deployable; 4.7 across 15 reviews
VapiTeams building voice agents fastAgent orchestration (can plug in any TTS)Fights for the entry point, not the voice: it uses your models as parts; 4.9 across 25 reviews
Rask AITeams localising videoDubbing plus subtitles plus multi-language distributionTakes the dubbing layer; 4.8 across 28 reviews; a narrower but deeper specialist
Hyperscaler TTS (Polly / Google Cloud)Enterprises already on the cloudGeneral TTS billed per characterThe substitute named in reviews: stable, cheap, no new vendor to sign, but not chasing human likeness

Conclusion: its position is unusual - it is sold to others as a part (orchestration layers such as Vapi plug its models in) while also selling the whole machine (Agents). So its rivals are not only lookalikes but also the platforms that treat it as a component.

extra_en.title: Competitors' technical base
extra_en.body:
Only what holds up: own base per the site and docs, rival bases per their PH one-liners and public positioning; milliseconds, parameter counts and prices are never guessed.

  • ElevenLabs: in-house TTS / STT / music / dubbing models plus voice library plus agent orchestration plus API / MCP. The seam is model generations: every version bump (v3 to v4) means old content must be regenerated to sound current, which is both stickiness and cost.
  • Deepgram: a speech platform born in ASR, transcription is home turf and TTS a follow-on; the edge is mature APIs and developer trust.
  • Cartesia: an in-house real-time speech model built around latency; [inferred] in phone support and live conversation this kind of base decides experience more than extra naturalness does.
  • Fish Audio: open-source TTS plus hosting, self-deployable; its moat presses on itself, since open source anchors the price.
  • Hyperscaler TTS: lives inside existing bills and catalogues with zero acquisition cost; technically it chases availability and compliance rather than human likeness.

[inferred] The real moat in this category is not whether it can generate - it is whether one voice stays the same person across text, language and session. That comes from data and evaluation systems, not parameter counts. It also explains why the most concrete complaints in reviews are all about inconsistency.

extra_en.title: Transferable opportunities (my judgement)
extra_en.body:
Four, ordered by whether one person can build them, not by imagination.

  1. Translate credits into finished minutes: show how many minutes this generation costs and how many clips the balance still buys, and offer alternatives near the limit (faster model, shorter text). Lightest - copy and estimation logic, a one-person week.
  2. A dedicated Chinese model tier: separate evaluation and tuning for tones, particles, phrasing and mixed Chinese-English reading, accent options, pricing aligned with local rivals. Most valuable - Chinese is one of the largest content-production markets, and general multilingual models fail exactly at sounding like a foreigner reading Chinese.
  3. Productise the licence: bind every cloned voice to usage rights (commercial, redistribution, term) and provenance, transferable and rev-shared. Heaviest, but the hardest for free open source to match.
  4. Paste-and-preview dubbing loop: chain dubbing with lip-sync and editing so users do not carry material elsewhere to assemble it. That is the step from material to finished good, and the clearest product gap today.

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation
extra_en.body:
Money comes out of three pockets, and the window is narrowing.

Whose pocket: budgets previously paid to voice actors, studios and localisation vendors - in essence it replaces the labour of a human voice. Creators pay $22 a month to avoid booking a booth; enterprises sign annual contracts to avoid hiring.

How long it lasts: the window is narrowing. Open-source and hyperscaler TTS are turning can generate into a free default, leaving premium on the last stretch of sounding human plus ecosystem. Its own answer is to shift weight toward Agents - from selling content per character to selling service per minute.

Why it gets paid: model lead, attention from 29 launches, API / MCP becoming other products' default voice, and enterprise logos. Lose one of the four and the price does not hold.

Traffic has three feeds: output-borne spread (content made with these voices carries the question), model launches (every release is a PH and media event) and developer directories (API, MCP, cloud markets). Monetisation has three layers: subscriptions (breadth), usage and concurrency (thickness), enterprise contracts and compliance (depth).

The weakest beam: the gap between credits and the monthly mental model - every 1-star review lives there; add one more layer: in Chinese it is merely one of many languages, while local rivals are cheaper and smoother.
